messages:
michelle: quick question — I have a work trip next week and need overnight backup care for 2 nights. what's the process for the travel-related overnight care stipend? can we get an advance or do we submit for reimbursement? :airplane:

andrew: hey michelle — we do reimburse for overnight backup care tied to business travel. standard policy is up to $250/night (max 3 nights per trip) if you use a licensed provider or agency. receipts required. :money_with_wings:

michelle: okay thanks. what about using a neighbor or friend (non-licensed) for overnight coverage?

people-ops-bot: FYI: policy link — https://intranet.redwood.example/hr/backup-care (internal only).

jen: short answer: neighbor/friend is usually not eligible for the stipend. we require either a registered caregiving service, licensed daycare that offers overnight services, or an agency invoice. exception possible for emergency single-night coverage with manager + people-ops pre-approval.

michelle: got it. is there an option for an advance? paying agency upfront might be tight.

andrew: we can do a payroll advance in special cases. please submit a quick request via People Ops form and cc your manager. the form asks for trip dates, provider name, estimated amount. once approved, we process advance as a separate payroll item (not taxable if used for legitimate care and receipts submitted).

michelle: how do I submit receipts? is it Expensify or direct upload?

jen: expense flow: Expensify preferred. if you can't use Expensify (international vendors sometimes block), email receipts to people-ops@redwood.com with subject: "Overnight care reimb - <YourName> - <TripDate>". include invoice or itemized receipt and provider business registration if available.

andrew: quick paste of what we need: 
```
- Provider name & contact
- Dates of overnight coverage
- Itemized invoice/receipt
- Proof of payment (card statement ok)
- If using neighbor exception: manager approval + emergency note
```

michelle: any tax implications if provider is local/self-employed? I'm in the UK office; worried about local reporting.

jen: good question. for US employees it's generally non-taxable if it's a business-related reimbursement with receipts. for international employees, tax treatment can vary. people-ops will coordinate with payroll/tax for any country-specific reporting. for the UK, we usually treat it as a reimbursement but might need a payroll post if HMRC rules require. include country in the form.

michelle: perfect. last q — can I pre-authorize a provider so I don't need emergency approvals?

andrew: yes — you can add a provider to an "approved backup list" by sending provider details + business registration to people-ops. we’ll vet and add them for future trips (saves you the exception step). allow 3 business days for vetting.

michelle: awesome — thanks everyone. submitting the form now. :raised_hands:

sara: quick note: michelle — if you need help filling the form, ping me and I can review before you send.

michelle: will do — thanks sara!
